newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks close higher on restructuring hopes.
newsitem.headline: China stocks close higher on restructuring hopes.

text.p: Chinese stocks closed higher on Monday as selected A shares for domestic investors and foreign currency B shares were buoyed by bargain hunting and expectations of restructuring plans, brokers said.
But many investors kept to the sidelines waiting for more companies to report their interim results and for the B share listing of Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd in Shanghai on Tuesday.

"Institutions were bargain hunting at low levels for heavily weighted shares in the index and that pushed the market up today," said a broker. "But the short-term trend will depend on the debut of Zhenhua Port."
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index closed up 0.594 point or 0.80 percent to 74.384 while the Shenzhen B share index gained a meagre 0.03 point to 130.89.
Shanghai's A share index was up 7.79 points or 0.62 percent to 1,256.271 while the Shenzhen A share index added 4.53 points or 1.11 percent to 413.99.
On the nation's major market, Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical Co was the second most active B share issue as it benefited from talk of a restructuring. It rose $0.006 or 2.46 percent to $0.250.
Such talk was helped by a statement from Yizheng Chemical Fibre that government authorities were studying a merger with other chemical firms.
Yizheng's A shares were up 0.03 yuan to 5.13 yuan ($0.618) after a suspension during the morning session. The company's H shares in Hong Kong were also buoyed by the announcement.
Huaxin Cement was the top B share performer in Shanghai as it climbed $0.01 or 7.69 percent to $0.140.

Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle was the most active issue, as 1.1 million shares changed hands, though it ended unchanged at $0.434. After the market close it announced first-half profits surged 147.7 percent.
Newly listed A share Chongqing Three Gorges Water Conservancy and Electric Power also put in a strong performance, closing at 14.29 yuan compared to the issue price of 6.38 yuan.
On the nation's southern bourse of Shenzhen, an advance in television tube maker Shenzhen SEG helped lift the B share index. SEG finished HK$0.47 or 9.75 percent higher at HK$5.29.
Market newcomer Bengang Steel was the most active B share issue, rising HK$0.06 to HK$2.13. It has traded well below its offer price of HK$2.38 since its listing early last month.
